# Ribbon Planning Tab

## How To Build

A RibbonPlanningTab should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A RibbonPlanningTab should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../../theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

The ribbon's Planning tab: the commands for planning work before it is sent, to be added.

## Description

The Planning tab of the ribbon, between Project and Code. It takes no mode's colour: its label is in the tab row's own colour, as Project's and Application's are.

## Groups

None yet. Opened alone, the command area reads "No commands yet", as the ribbon says of a tab with no commands, and opened beside other tabs, it adds nothing to the command area.
18:A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says more. Its tabs are, in order: Project, Planning, Code, Spec, and Application. The window always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.
22:<Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+2> opening Planning and <Alt+5> Application. Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no tooltip.

content.text:
I added the ribbon's Planning tab between Project and Code. As the spec describes it, the tab has no commands yet:

- **Colour:** its label uses the tab row's own colour, like Project and Application, since it isn't tied to a mode.
- **Commands:** opened alone, the command area reads "No commands yet". Opened beside other tabs, it adds nothing.
- **Shortcuts:** Alt+1 to Alt+5 now cover all five tabs, so Alt+2 opens Planning and Alt+5 opens Application.

The tab lives in a new `src/ribbon/planning_tab.rs`. I updated the Alt-number test for the new order and added Planning to the per-tab test, which checks the "No commands yet" line.

Those tests pass. Two other main window tests, `restart_from_within_the_window_never_panics` and `quitting_while_a_task_runs_asks_first`, failed when run with the full module. Each has failed intermittently before, and the restart one passed twice when run on its own.
